blueprints.name: Relaycraft
blueprints.tagline: Move business data across systems, with every transformation visible.
blueprints.purpose: A compact integration studio for assembling connector-based data flows, mapping fields, previewing transformations and running a seeded sync job.
blueprints.audience: Operations engineers, integration specialists and teams connecting business systems.
blueprints.ux: A node-and-mapping workbench with a left connector rail, central pipeline canvas, lower record preview and a right run inspector.
screens: Pipeline canvas with ordered source, transform and destination nodes
Run history with row counts and error details
flows: Choose a source and destination connector from seeded systems.
Add a transform step and map source fields to destination fields.
Preview the first sample records and inspect unmapped fields.
Run a deterministic local sync simulation and review processed, skipped and failed rows.
blueprints.model: Connector, Connection, Pipeline, PipelineStep, FieldMapping, SampleRecord, SyncRun. Store connector capabilities separately from credential references; demo data must contain no real secrets.
blueprints.guard: No live connectors, credentials, network requests or writes to external systems. The run is a deterministic local simulation. Never display real API keys or connection secrets.
prompts: Implement a typed pipeline graph model with connector, transform and destination step validation.
Build a mapping service that previews deterministic sample-record transformations and reports unmapped or invalid fields.
Add run history, retry semantics for seeded failed rows and unit tests for mapping edge cases.

blueprints.name: Mobiary
blueprints.tagline: A compact mobile companion for the moments between meetings.
blueprints.purpose: A mobile-first personal field journal prototype demonstrating native-feeling navigation, widgets, quick capture and a responsive companion dashboard.
blueprints.audience: Mobile product teams, field workers and users who capture short notes while moving.
blueprints.ux: A device-first prototype: realistic phone bezel and touch-sized screen on the left, feature configuration and widget controls on the right.
screens: Mobile home with daily focus and quick actions
Capture view for a note, photo placeholder or voice memo
flows: Switch between Home, Activity and Profile tabs in the device preview.
Create a quick note and see it appear in the activity list.
Add or remove home widgets from the companion controls.
Toggle compact mode and notification preference.
blueprints.model: UserProfile, JournalEntry, MobileWidget, DevicePreference, ActivityItem. Store UI state and demo entries locally in the prototype.
blueprints.guard: The device is a responsive web mockup, not an installed native or hybrid application. Camera and microphone actions are simulated; no device permissions or data collection.
prompts: Build a mobile-first navigation shell with accessible touch targets and safe-area-aware layout.
Implement offline-first journal entries with local persistence and queued sync state.
Create widget configuration and device capability adapters with tests for mobile and desktop breakpoints.

blueprints.name: Canvasmith Desktop
blueprints.tagline: A focused desktop workspace for building and organizing visual assets.
blueprints.purpose: A desktop application shell prototype with project navigation, asset thumbnails, a central editing canvas and contextual property controls.
blueprints.audience: Designers, desktop-product teams and developers exploring native, Electron or Tauri application UX.
blueprints.ux: A dense desktop window with familiar native chrome, project sidebar, central canvas, inspector and bottom asset strip.
screens: Asset canvas with selection and zoom
flows: Select a project asset from the left sidebar.
Select a layer to inspect and edit its properties.
Change zoom and toggle the layer list.
Create an asset card and export a simulated preview.
blueprints.model: DesktopProject, Asset, Layer, Property, ExportPreset, RecentFile. Model window state and selected asset independently from persistent project data.
blueprints.guard: A browser-based desktop UI simulation only. It does not access the local filesystem, OS window manager, clipboard or native export APIs.
prompts: Create a cross-platform desktop shell with explicit platform abstraction boundaries for Electron and Tauri.
Implement typed project, asset and layer models with undoable inspector edits.
Add local file adapter interfaces and export-preset tests without coupling domain logic to the host runtime.

blueprints.name: Pagefoundry
blueprints.tagline: Shape a web experience, block by block.
blueprints.purpose: A browser-based website builder prototype with page navigation, a live page preview, block insertion and a right-side design inspector.
blueprints.audience: Small teams, designers and developers creating websites, SaaS pages and portals.
blueprints.ux: A visual web editor with a left page/block navigator, centered browser-like page canvas and inspector on the right.
screens: Live website canvas with selectable sections
flows: Switch between Home, Features and Pricing pages.
Select a hero, feature grid or CTA section in the preview.
Insert a new section and change its headline or background theme.
Toggle preview mode and publish a simulated build.
blueprints.model: Site, Page, Section, Block, ThemeToken, PublishVersion. Represent page structure as ordered blocks with schema-defined editable properties.
blueprints.guard: The builder edits local demo state only. Publishing is simulated; no external hosting, analytics, form submissions or third-party services.
prompts: Implement a schema-driven page builder with reusable block types and serializable page documents.
Create an editor state model with selection, insertion, deletion and undo/redo operations.
Build responsive rendering and a deterministic static-export pipeline with page-schema tests.

blueprints.name: Termforge
blueprints.tagline: A command workspace for repeatable work, not just a prompt.
blueprints.purpose: A terminal-native workspace prototype combining a simulated shell, command history, task shortcuts and a compact system status panel.
blueprints.audience: Developers, platform engineers and technical users who prefer keyboard-driven interfaces.
blueprints.ux: A terminal-first dark TUI with split panes: command console, task launcher and session metadata.
screens: Task launcher for build, test and deploy routines
flows: Run safe predefined commands from the prompt or shortcut list.
Use help, ls, pwd, git status, npm test and date to inspect seeded output.
Select a command snippet to populate the prompt.
Clear the terminal or switch between workspace tabs.
blueprints.model: TerminalSession, CommandHistory, CommandSnippet, Workspace, EnvironmentStatus, CommandResult. Commands must be parsed against a strict demo allowlist.
blueprints.guard: This is a browser simulation. It must never invoke a host shell, execute arbitrary commands, read files, access SSH or expose real environment variables.
prompts: Implement a command parser with an explicit allowlist and deterministic output fixtures; reject all unknown commands.
Build a keyboard-accessible terminal history with command recall, clear and shortcut snippets.
Add multi-session persistence and tests proving that no command can reach host process execution.

blueprints.name: Luma Space
blueprints.tagline: Compose spatial experiences from scenes, anchors and interactions.
blueprints.purpose: An XR scene-composition prototype for arranging spatial anchors, switching between AR/VR/MR modes and inspecting object placement in a stylized viewport.
blueprints.audience: XR designers, spatial-computing developers and teams prototyping immersive product concepts.
blueprints.ux: An immersive dark scene editor with a large spatial viewport, floating scene object list and contextual transform inspector.
screens: Scene viewport and camera mode selector
Transform inspector for position, scale and rotation
flows: Switch between AR, VR and MR preview modes.
Select scene objects and inspect their transform values.
Add a new spatial anchor to the scene.
Adjust the world scale and run a local interaction preview.
blueprints.model: XRScene, SceneObject, SpatialAnchor, Transform3D, Interaction, PreviewMode. Keep coordinates in a typed 3D vector and units explicit.
blueprints.guard: The viewport is a visual 3D-style mockup, not a real XR session. No camera passthrough, tracking, eye data, biometric input or physical-world mapping. Do not claim AR safety or spatial accuracy.
prompts: Implement a scene graph with stable object IDs, parent-child transforms and explicit meter units.
Build an XR preview-state controller for AR, VR and MR modes without requiring a hardware runtime.
Add scene serialization, anchor validation and tests for transform composition and scale boundaries.

blueprints.name: Sensepath Lab
blueprints.tagline: Prototype the interface between human intent and machine response.
blueprints.purpose: An interaction research workbench for reviewing input modalities, running a simulated task and comparing accessibility and usability signals.
blueprints.audience: HCI researchers, product designers, accessibility practitioners and prototyping teams.
blueprints.ux: A research lab layout with modality selector, task-stage display, calibration controls and a measured-session summary.
screens: Speech, gesture, gaze, haptic and alternative interaction panels
flows: Choose a modality and inspect its requirements and feedback loop.
Run a short local task simulation for the selected modality.
Adjust sensitivity or feedback settings.
Save an observation and compare the session summary.
blueprints.model: Modality, InteractionProfile, Calibration, TaskScenario, SessionRun, Observation. Track synthetic timing and completion events without collecting real user signals.
blueprints.guard: All modality activity is simulated. No microphone, camera, eye tracking, brain-computer interface, haptic device or biometric input is accessed. Sample metrics are illustrative and not clinical or scientific evidence.
prompts: Design a modality adapter interface that separates device-specific input from normalized interaction events.
Implement synthetic task scenarios and session metrics for keyboard, speech, gaze and gesture prototypes.
Add accessible modality settings, consent gates for any future device integration and unit tests around normalized events.

blueprints.name: LingoDesk
blueprints.tagline: Translate at scale without losing the voice of the product.
blueprints.purpose: A translation-management and CAT-workbench prototype with locale selection, segment editing, terminology suggestions and QA checks.
blueprints.audience: Localization managers, translators, product teams and language-service providers.
blueprints.ux: A focused translation editor: project/locale rail, source-target segment table, glossary sidebar and progress header.
flows: Choose a target locale and filter segments by state.
Edit a target segment and save the draft.
Insert a glossary term or translation-memory suggestion.
Run local QA checks for empty targets, placeholders and terminology consistency.
blueprints.model: LocalizationProject, Locale, MessageKey, TranslationSegment, GlossaryTerm, TranslationMemoryEntry, QAIssue. Preserve stable message keys and placeholder tokens.
blueprints.guard: Translations and QA are illustrative seeded examples. No machine-translation provider, external localization service or production content is contacted. Never silently rewrite approved translations.
prompts: Implement a locale-aware message catalog with stable keys, plural forms and placeholder validation.
Build a translation editor with draft, review and approved states plus glossary and translation-memory suggestions.
Add QA checks for missing strings, placeholders, length constraints and term consistency with unit tests.

blueprints.name: Clearpath Audit
blueprints.tagline: Make accessibility visible, testable and part of the build.
blueprints.purpose: An accessibility audit and assistive-preview prototype for triaging sample interface issues, previewing contrast and text settings, and recording remediation.
blueprints.audience: Accessibility specialists, QA teams, designers and product owners.
blueprints.ux: A quality-audit console with issue severity rail, live page preview and a detailed remediation panel.
screens: Sample page with contrast and typography controls
Issue detail with affected component and suggested fix
flows: Filter audit items by severity and select an issue.
Inspect the corresponding component in the preview.
Toggle a high-contrast or enlarged-text preview.
Mark a sample issue resolved and re-run the local checklist.
blueprints.model: AccessibilityAudit, AuditIssue, ComponentReference, Remediation, PreviewSetting, AuditRun. Track WCAG criterion references only when the implementation spec includes verified mapping.
blueprints.guard: This is a sample issue triage concept, not an automated conformance certificate. Passing visible demo checks does not prove WCAG compliance. Do not infer disability or user health from interactions.
prompts: Implement an accessibility issue model with severity, component references, WCAG mapping metadata and remediation state.
Build accessible preview toggles for contrast, text scale, focus visibility and reduced motion.
Add deterministic audit fixtures and unit tests; explicitly label heuristic checks as non-conformance evidence.

blueprints.name: Restorepoint
blueprints.tagline: Know what is protected, and how quickly you can recover it.
blueprints.purpose: A backup operations and recovery-planning prototype with job status, restore points, retention visibility and a guided restore simulation.
blueprints.audience: IT administrators, infrastructure teams and operations leads responsible for business continuity.
blueprints.ux: A dark operational console with backup job rail, recovery timeline and a guided restore target inspector.
screens: Protected workloads and backup job list
Recovery plan preview and simulated restore run
flows: Select a protected workload and inspect its recent snapshots.
Choose a recovery point on the timeline.
Preview the destination and selected restore scope.
Run a local verification simulation and review recovery status.
blueprints.model: ProtectedWorkload, BackupJob, RecoveryPoint, RetentionPolicy, RestorePlan, VerificationRun. Distinguish backup completion, integrity verification and restore readiness.
blueprints.guard: No real data is read, copied, deleted, overwritten or restored. Restore actions are simulations against seeded metadata. Never imply that a real recovery point is valid without independent verification.
prompts: Implement backup-job and recovery-point domain models with explicit states for completed, verified and restore-ready.
Build a retention timeline and restore-plan preview that requires scope and destination confirmation.
Add deterministic verification simulations, audit events and tests for stale or incomplete recovery points.
